correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact published generator normalization. The complex-number chord identity shows that generator directions are indexed by \(i+j\) modulo \(n\), giving exactly \(n\) equally spaced direction classes. For odd \(n\), multiplication by two is invertible and all classes have the common chord-length sum \(\cot(\pi/(2n))\), forcing a regular \(2n\)-gon. For even \(n\), the two residue parities give the exact sums \(2\cot(\pi/n)\) and \(2\csc(\pi/n)\). The two support numbers follow from adjacent-edge geometry, which proves cyclicity and the area formula. Unequal alternating sides give the exact even-order symmetry group.

originality.rationale: The primary full text was inspected at the sweep-polytope definition, normal-fan theorem, and permutahedral-projection theorem, and contains no regular-polygon specialization. Candidate-specific indexed searches covered regular polygon, sweep polytope, shellotope, pairwise-difference zonotope, chord zonotope, alternating edge lengths, regularity, area, and perimeter formulations. No source was located that states the odd-regular/even-alternating classification or its exact metric formulas. A previously checked general radius theorem for vertex-transitive zonotopes was compared privately for overlap; it concerns inradius, circumradius, and tangent facets, not the side-orbit, regularity, symmetry-order, perimeter, or area statement accepted here.

value.rationale: Sweep polytopes are the primary source's canonical geometric model for sweeps and permutahedral shadows, and a regular polygon is the maximally symmetric planar input. The theorem identifies a structural parity transition rather than an arbitrary numerical invariant: odd input unexpectedly gains enough symmetry to become a regular \(2n\)-gon, whereas even input retains two distinct metric edge orbits. The exact side lengths, perimeter, area, cyclicity, and symmetry orders give a complete Euclidean shape description of this natural family.
